subject: Multi-cloud private offer: margin alignment and invoice path (Azure + GCP)
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Avery Cloud <avery@cloudledger.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-cloud private offer: margin alignment and invoice path (Azure + GCP)

Hi Avery —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our discussion, I’m sending a compact summary of how Redwood would structure the private offer across Azure and GCP and the expected channel passback for your reseller network. Attached is a one-page PO summary and a draft of the private-offer terms for signature.

Two items we need to lock to move to procurement:
- Confirm the final net list price per reserved GPU hour for the Azure private offer (we proposed $0.68/hr with a 10% partner pass-through).
- Confirm the GCP SKU mapping: CloudLedger wants the same committed discount applied to the GCP listing; we proposed an equivalent $/vCPU-hour bucket and a 12% channel uplift to cover distributor fees.

If both are OK, procurement can sign the DocuSign and we’ll start onboarding (we can support staggered activation if you want Azure live first).

Attachments: CL-PO-summary-20270729.xlsx, redline-private-offer.pdf

Next step: can procurement confirm the invoice path (direct to CloudLedger or pass-through to your distributor)? If they want distributor invoicing, we’ll need the distributor legal name and tax ID to include in the PO.

Thanks —
Markus

--
Markus Klein
Head of Cloud Partnerships | Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.com
From: Avery Cloud <avery@cloudledger.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@cloudledger.com
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 13:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-cloud private offer: margin alignment and invoice path (Azure + GCP)

Markus —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. A few clarifications from our side before procurement will circulate:

1) Azure net list price — the $0.68/hr is broadly acceptable but we need to maintain a 5% floor on partner pass-through (legal/finance requirement). Can Redwood accept a constraint: partner pass-through between 5–12% (we prefer 10%)?

2) GCP SKU mapping — finance needs a short mapping table that ties your GCP SKU to our internal consumption buckets (dev/staging/prod). The attached summary is a good start; can you provide the explicit SKU equivalences and the estimated monthly spend per bucket?

3) Distributor invoicing — we will ask procure to confirm whether they want direct invoicing or pass-through. If pass-through, distributor details (name, tax ID, contact) will be sent.

Also, Laura from our procurement team may send a redline to the private-offer doc.

Thanks,
Avery

Avery Cloud
Head of Cloud Operations, CloudLedger
avery@cloudledger.com
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Avery Cloud <avery@cloudledger.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 15:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-cloud private offer: margin alignment and invoice path (Azure + GCP)

Thanks Avery — noted. Quick responses inline:

1) Partner pass-through floor: we can accept the 5–12% constraint on the Azure offer. We’ll set the default at 10% with the contract clause that allows a 5% minimum if CloudLedger requests it in writing.

2) SKU mapping: attached is an updated worksheet that maps Redwood GCP SKUs to the CloudLedger buckets (worksheet tab: SKU_mapping). We included estimated monthly spend per bucket using your dev/staging/prod breakdown from the call. Please check numbers — they’re intentionally conservative.

3) Distributor invoicing: understood — we’ll wait for procurement to confirm. If pass-through, we need the distributor legal name and remit address for the invoice sub-account.

I’m copying Ben and Camila to confirm the billing implications and whether this requires separate invoice streams per cloud (Ben), and to confirm SSO/entitlement mapping for GCP (Camila).

Markus

--
Markus Klein
Head of Cloud Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Avery Cloud <avery@cloudledger.com>, procure@cloudledger.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Multi-cloud private offer: margin alignment and invoice path (Azure + GCP)

Avery / team —

I attached a concise redline to the private-offer PDF focusing only on commercial and invoicing language (see redline-private-offer.pdf). Key changes we made to keep approvals moving:
- Defined partner pass-through as a percentage of list per invoice cycle with a maximum of 12% and a minimum of 5% (aligns with Markus’s note).
- Added a clause that allows CloudLedger to choose distributor invoicing on a per-invoice basis with 30 days notice; Redwood will not be held liable for distributor billing errors if CloudLedger elects pass-through.
- Clarified that GCP SKU equivalence is for billing and quota mapping only; any residual rounding differences will be reconciled monthly and credited to CloudLedger.

Ben — quick question for you: if CloudLedger elects distributor invoicing, do we need to set up a second invoice stream in our billing system or can we use the existing account with a distributor tag? If a second stream is required, estimate how long to provision.

Avery — procurement should confirm the distributor legal name and remit details; once we have that I’ll prepare a final DocuSign packet with the agreed pass-through percentage and SKU mapping attachments.

Thanks,
Laura

Attachment: redline-private-offer.pdf
--
Laura Bennett
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Avery Cloud <avery@cloudledger.com>, procure@cloudledger.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Multi-cloud private offer: margin alignment and invoice path (Azure + GCP)

Laura / Markus / Avery —

Short answer on billing: we can support distributor pass-through without provisioning a full separate invoice stream. Operational approach: create a distributor remit tag on the CloudLedger account; invoices that elect pass-through will include the distributor remit block and a separate accounting code. This requires a day for ops to enable the tag and 3 business days to validate EDI/banking details if your distributor needs automated remit.

If CloudLedger needs a fully separate legal billing entity (i.e., invoices made out to the distributor instead of CloudLedger), that’s a heavier change and will require AP/finance sign-off (estimate 2–3 weeks). For now recommend the remit-tag approach so we can sign and go live quickly.

Avery — if procurement confirms they want the remit-tag flow, send distributor details and we’ll enable the tag immediately. I’ll also add the monthly rounding reconciliation note to the billing playbook.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Manager, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
